abhay-gaidhane:
ABHAY M. GAIDHANE

Dr. Abhay M. Gaidhane is a physician, public health researcher, academic leader, and global health innovator with experience in public health, primary healthcare, early childhood development, research capacity strengthening, and translating evidence into scalable health solutions. He authored 200+ peer-reviewed publications and was consistently recognised among Top 2% of Scientists globally in the Stanford–Elsevier ranking, including in 2025.

He is Director, Public Health & Epidemiological Research at Datta Meghe Institute of Higher Education and Research (DMIHER), India. He has held several leadership positions at DMIHER, including Dean of Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College and Honorary Director of the School of Epidemiology and Public Health. He is a Director of a Section 8 Company and a co-founder of startups Stepping-Stones LLP.

His research focuses on delivery systems, community-based interventions, early-stage innovations, evidence generation, monitoring and evaluation, and primary healthcare, with particular emphasis on early childhood development, nutrition, mental health, and rural health. He served as Principal Investigator or Co-PI on major projects supported by ICMR, BIRAC, Grand Challenges Canada, India Alliance, Wellcome Trust, and AusAID. He also contributes to research translation and innovation through the BIRAC BioNEST Bio-Incubator, the Technical Resource Hub for evidence-based guideline development supported by DHR.

A strong advocate for equitable global health partnerships, his work bridges research, education, innovation, and implementation.
andreas-hovener:
Dr. Andreas Hövener is a Senior Lecturer at FH Münster University of Applied Sciences in Germany, where he teaches English and Social Sciences and serves as Internationalization Coordinator for the Department of Health. His work focuses on intercultural communication, internationalization and innovative approaches to learning in higher education.

He has undertaken further training in intercultural communication and intercultural training and is particularly interested in innovative teaching formats such as COIL (Collaborative Online International Learning) and BIP (Blended Intensive Programmes).

His current research interests include the effectiveness of collaborative online learning and short-term international exchange formats, particularly in developing intercultural competence.
bulat-ziganshin:
Bulat A. Ziganshin, MD, PhD

Dr. Bulat Ziganshin is the Executive Director of the Global Health Academy at Northwell Health, Danbury Hospital, and the Christian J. Trefz Family Endowed Chair in Global Health.

Dr. Ziganshin received his Medical Doctor (MD) Degree from Kazan State Medical University (Kazan, Russia) in 2007 followed by clinical training in General Surgery through an Internship program (2008) and a two-year clinical residency program in Cardiovascular Surgery in (2010), both at the Department of Surgical Diseases # 2 of Kazan State Medical University. In April 2017, Dr. Ziganshin was awarded a PhD degree in Pharmacology from Kazan State Medical University, and in 2024 a PhD degree in Genetics and Development from Columbia University.

Dr. Ziganshin has a long-lasting interest in global health (GH). From 2006 until 2015, he was employed as the Senior Officer for International Medical Exchange programs at the GH Center of Kazan State Medical University. Since 2016, he has directed the Danbury Hospital GH Elective Program for students of the American University of the Caribbean and Ross University School of Medicine, furthering curriculum development, research projects, and program growth.

Dr. Ziganshin has published over 200 scientific manuscripts in peer-reviewed journals, as well as one textbook on management of aortic disease, 19 chapters in other textbooks, and co-authored five drug reference books. His research interests include aortic disease, genetics and genomics, cardiac surgery, pharmacology, and global health.
shalote-chipamaunga-bamu:
Shalote Chipamaunga – Brief biography

Shalote Chipamaunga is a visionary Health Professions Education specialist with over a decade of transformative leadership driving innovation in medical and health sciences education. From her roots in nursing and adult education to earning her PhD in Medical Education, she has dedicated her career to turning institutional gaps into accredited programs, sustainable faculty development, and powerful global health partnerships. Her work has strengthened undergraduate and postgraduate health professions education at the University of Zimbabwe, contributed to medical curriculum transformation under Education 5.0, and helped develop a new generation of health professions education leaders. By championing student-centered learning and mentoring the next generation of healthcare pioneers, Dr. Chipamaunga has built a legacy that elevates global health systems.

Dr Shalote Chipamaunga holds a PhD in Medical Education (University of the Witwatersrand), Masters and Bachelors degree in Adult Education and Diploma in Nursing Education (University of Zimbabwe), and Nursing and Midwifery (Zimbabwe).
zahir-quazi:
Dr. Syed Zahiruddin Quazi is the Executive Director, Directorate of Research & Innovation, Datta Meghe Institute of Higher Education and Research (DMIHER), India, and is listed among the top 2% of scientists globally in the Stanford–Elsevier ranking. He leads and supports multidisciplinary research and innovation across DMIHER, with expertise in spanning global health, health technology, maternal and child health, nutrition, early childhood development, clinical translational research, and complex health interventions.

He has fostered interdisciplinary collaborations and contributed to mobilizing INR 450+ million in research funding from national and international agencies. He has authored more than 250 peer-reviewed publications, including work published in The Lancet, Nature, PLOS, and BMJ.

Dr. Quazi has also contributed to health-policy and evidence-informed initiatives, including work associated with the WHO South-East Asia Region. Under his research leadership, DMIHER has strengthened its national research platforms through ICMR-INTENT, the Department of Health Research’s Multidisciplinary Research Unit, and Technical Resource Hub for evidence-based guideline development. His work emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration, responsible innovation, mentorship, and translating promising technologies from research into meaningful clinical and healthcare applications.
auemphon-mordmuang:
Assoc. Prof. Dr. Auemphon (Prym) Mordmuang, Ph.D. is an Associate Professor of Microbiology and Assistant Dean for International Affairs at the School of Medicine, Walailak University, Thailand.

My work integrates clinical microbiology, infectious diseases, maternal health, and natural products.

My research and teaching, I have experience in health promotion and policy-oriented initiatives, with an emphasis on connecting research evidence with community health needs and preventive health strategies. My work reflects an interdisciplinary approach that integrates biomedical research, health education, environmental health, and health promotion to support evidence-informed policies and medical education.
aida-mencia-ripley:
Aída Mencía-Ripley, Ph.D., CPsychol

Vice Rector for Research and Innovation

UNESCO Chair Intersectional Gender Studies

Unibe

Chartered Psychologist, British Psychological Society

Salazar Award 2017, Interamerican Psychological Society

Titular de la Carrera Nacional de Investigadores

Quisqueyanos para el Mundo Award, Ministry of Foreign Affairs

M.A. in Psychology, The New School for Social Research

M.A. and Ph.D. in Clinical Psychology, St. John’s University

She has focused her work in creating the research infrastructure and research policies at UNIBE. Author of books, book chapters and papers in peer reviewed journals. She has also presented her research at international conferences. Her research focuses on the psychology of women, mental health, monitoring and evaluation, and higher education.
alexander-bazarchyan:
Dr. Alexander Bazarchyan is a public health professional with over two decades of experience. He has served as Director of the National Institute of Health of Armenia since 2014, contributing to the advancement of public health and healthcare education in Armenia. Previously, he served as Deputy Director of NIH and Head of the Public Health Department at the Ministry of Health.

Dr. Bazarchyan has managed major international initiatives, including the G2G USAID project and UNAIDS programs. He has coordinated numerous nationwide surveys on tobacco, alcohol, drugs, nutrition, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, immunization, and other public health priorities. He has authored more than 100 publications.

He has been actively involved in tobacco control in Armenia, including the development of the Tobacco Control Legislative package adopted in 2020. In 2004, he received the World Health Organization Director-General’s Award for outstanding contribution to tobacco control.

He is also involved in healthcare education reforms, including Continuing Medical Education, physician licensing, and residency programs.

Dr. Bazarchyan received his medical degree from Yerevan State Medical Institute in 1991, completed residencies in Internal Medicine and Epidemiology, and received his PhD in 2003.
anastasia-zholud: Anastasia Zholud is the Global Health Electives Coordinator at the Majid Sadigh, MD Global Health Academy, where she oversees international medical student placements across partner sites spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean, and the Caucasus. She manages the full arc of the program — from interviews and pre-departure orientation to site coordination, student support, and outcome evaluation — ensuring that each elective is both educationally meaningful and logistically sound. A certified AFS Qualified Facilitator in intercultural dialogue, Anastasia brings a deep commitment to cultural humility, reciprocity, and the kind of partnership that goes beyond placement logistics to build lasting, equitable relationships with host institutions and communities.
andrea-green: Andrea E. Green, MDCM, FAAP is an Emeritus Professor of Pediatrics at the University of Vermont (UVM) Larner College of Medicine (LCOM). She is the Co-Chair of Arts@Larner an initiative which brings humanities into the LCOM curriculum. She is the Former Director of the Pediatric New American Program and Pediatric Global Health at the Galisano Children’s Hospital at UVM. Her clinical duties and scholarship are in providing care to children in immigrant families (CIF). Areas of academic focus regarding CIF include mental health and multigenerational trauma, non-medical drivers of health, health literacy, community and medical care coordination, and autism.  She has authored peer reviewed primary research, commentary and policy and spoken regionally and nationally on pediatric immigrant healthcare.  She is the current Vice President of the Vermont Chapter of the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) and the Past President of the national AAP Council on Community Pediatrics.  She is actively engaged in advocacy work to support Vermont’s immigrant and pediatric populations.
vo-ngoc-anh-tho:
Vo Ngoc Anh Tho, MD, MSc, is Head of the Visa Medical Department and the External Relations Unit at Cho Ray Hospital in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. An infectious diseases specialist, she previously served as Deputy Head of the Tropical Diseases Department. In 2018, she was a Global Health Scholar at Norwalk Hospital in Connecticut, where she spent three months learning about infectious diseases, intensive care, and wound care. During the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020–2021, she led Cho Ray Hospital’s COVID-19 Treatment Unit.

Throughout her clinical career, Dr. Tho has provided hands-on teaching and mentorship to colleagues training in tropical diseases and toxicology at Cho Ray Hospital. Her current clinical and research interests focus on preventing and managing infections before and after kidney transplantation. She also serves as Secretary of the Ho Chi Minh City Infectious Diseases Society. Her work brings together clinical care, teaching, research, and international collaboration to improve care for patients with complex infections.
arinda-vivian: Dr. Arinda Vivian is an associate consultant psychiatrist based in Kampala, Uganda, with clinical and research interests in child and adolescent mental health, caregiver wellbeing, and community mental health. She recently completed a Master of Medicine in Psychiatry at Makerere University, where her research examined the prevalence and factors associated with depression among primary caregivers of children with autism spectrum disorder in Uganda, one of the first studies to address this gap in the sub-Saharan African context. She is committed to expanding access to evidence-based psychiatric care in Uganda and the wider region.
arya-kale: Arya Kale (they/them) is a current fourth-year medical student at the University of Vermont Larner College of Medicine, born and raised in Michigan, U.S.A. to South Indian immigrants. While attending the University of Michigan, they led local environmental justice organizations focused on local public policy. After graduating with a degree in Spanish Language and Biochemistry, they moved to Berkeley, CA to develop online educational lessons for elementary school students in during the height of the COVID pandemic. During medical school, Arya rotated in for six weeks at el Hospital General de la Plaza de la Salud in Santo Domingo, the Dominican Republic, sparking a passion for global health. They have applied to Ob/Gyn residency and have an interest in advancing health equity, particularly at the intersection of global health and obstetric/gynecologic medicine.
baby-boy-benjamin-d-nebres:
Dr. Baby Boy Benjamin D. Nebres III President, Bicol University | Champion for Human-Centered Global Health Education

Dr. Baby Boy Benjamin D. Nebres III is the 9th President of Bicol University and the youngest in the University’s history to hold the position. An educator, researcher, innovator, and transformative public servant, he advances Bicol University’s vision as a “University for Humanity,” anchored on productive scholarship, collaborative service, transformative leadership, and sustainable societies. With extensive experience in educational leadership, community engagement, student development, research, and innovation, he has led national and regional higher education organizations and guided multidisciplinary initiatives with government and community partners. He holds 47 registered copyrights and nine industrial design patents, reflecting his commitment to educational innovation. His leadership centers on equitable education, community empowerment, global partnerships, and human-centered innovation for sustainable health and development.
catherine-nakibuule:
Dr. Catherine Nakibuule is a Ugandan Medical Doctor, public health professional, and health-care leader with experience spanning clinical medicine, health systems leadership, HIV programming, quality improvement and community health.

She serves as Medical Superintendent of St. Stephen’s Hospital Mpererwe, where she provides strategic and clinical leadership, mentors health-care teams, leads quality improvement initiatives, mobilizes resources, and strengthens partnerships to improve patient care.

Since 2018, Dr. Nakibuule has also served as HIV Project Coordinator, leading HIV care and treatment programming, TB screening, viral-load monitoring, retention, staff development, and quality improvement. Through focused planning, teamwork, mentorship, and use of data, she has contributed to improving HIV client linkage and TB screening. She holds a Master of Public Health from Makerere University, a Postgraduate Diploma in Project Planning and Management from Uganda Management Institute, and a Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery from Makerere University. Her professional interests include quality improvement,  Child Health, public health, HIV care, research and  strengthening health systems.
charles-herrick:
Dr. Herrick first joined Danbury Hospital in June 1998, having moved from Manhattan where he worked at Jacobi Medical Center in the Bronx.  Dr. Herrick became the Chair of Psychiatry at Danbury Hospital in October 2006, and chair of psychiatry for Western Connecticut Health Network in April, 2018.  He is now the Network Chair of Psychiatry for Nuvance Health Network.  He has worked in and overseen various programs at Danbury Hospital, including Consultation Services, Emergency Services, Inpatient Services, and Chemical Dependency Services. He has also served on numerous committees both for the hospital, the medical group, and at the state level, including the Quality Committee, Finance Committee, Compensation Committee, Ethics Committee, and The Behavioral Health Partnership Oversight Committee, which oversee the Medicaid services for behavioral Health in the state of Connecticut.

Dr. Herrick graduated from Southern Illinois University School of Medicine, completed his residency training in general psychiatry at Tufts, New England Medical Center Hospitals, and a fellowship in child and adolescent psychiatry at the University of California, San Francisco.  Dr. Herrick’s clinical experience has been diverse in terms of patient population, practice setting, and geographic location.  He has worked in Boston, San Francisco, and New York City before coming to Danbury. He has coauthored books on depression, bipolar disorder, alcoholism and smoking cessation for patients and their family members and has lectured on a variety of psychiatric and ethics topics to both medical audiences and the public.

Dr. Herrick is a member of the faculty at University of Vermont Medical College, Zucker School of Medicine, Ross University School of Medicine, American University of the Caribbean, and University of Medicine and Health Sciences, where he serves as clinical dean and chair of psychiatry.   Dr. Herrick assisted with the development of the Nuvance Health Psychiatry Residency Training Program, which began July, ’20 and is currently serving as the Associate Residency Training Program Director. Dr. Herrick has served on various boards, including the Regional Hospice of Western Connecticut, and the Newtown-Sandy Hook Community Foundation, which provides oversight of funding for the victims of Sandy Hook.
christa-zehle: Dr. Christa Zehle is the Senior Associate Dean for Medical Education at the Larner College of Medicine at the University of Vermont, and the Director of the University of Vermont Health Network Education. She is responsible for the delivery of the Larner College of Medicine medical education programs which includes admissions, curriculum at both our Vermont and Connecticut campuses, medical student services which support the academic success, personal wellness, career planning and professional development for all enrolled medical students, the Clinical Simulation Lab, the Teaching Academy, Continuing Medical and Interprofessional Education, and facilitating the collaboration of the educational missions of the Larner College of Medicine and the UVM Health Network. She is a sought-after mentor and has received several awards for teaching. In addition to her roles at Larner, she practices as a pediatric hospitalist and successfully founded the Pediatric Hospitalist Program at The University of Vermont Medical Center in 2003. She is a Master Teacher at the Teaching Academy, and a member of the Alpha Omega Alpha Honor Medical Society and the Gold Humanism in Medicine Honor Society. She serves as a fellow of the American Academy of Pediatrics, is a member of the American Medical Association (AMA) and the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC). Dr. Zehle actively participates in the AAMC Group on Student Affairs, Group on Educational Affairs, and Medical Education Senior Leaders group. She previously served as a member of the AAMC Committee on Student Affairs Student Wellbeing Working Group resulting in a publication in Academic Medicine titled A Guiding Model for Undergraduate Medical Education Well-Being Programs (2024) and currently serves as the chair for the AAMC Student Survey Committee.
christopher-muyshondt:
Christopher Muyshondt, MD:

Christopher Muyshondt, MD recently graduated this past August 2026 from the American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine. He will be applying to Emergency Medicine in the current 2026 Residency application cycle. He is originally from Austin, Texas with his father's side of the family being from El Salvador. Christopher took an interest in Global Health as his grandfather was a surgeon in El Salvador and he wanted to give back to Latin countries as a clinician himself, to honor his grandfather’s memory and his service. He did a Global Health rotation with Nuvance Health during his final year of medical school in the Dominican Republic and fell in love with this aspect of medicine. Christopher has since joined two separate Global Health Non-profit Organizations and plans to continue gaining experience in more countries across the world.
cladious-verenga:
Cladious Verenga:

Dr Cladious Verenga is a Zimbabwean obstetrician-gynaecologist, fetal medicine specialist, and medical educator. He is Deputy Head of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Sally Mugabe Central Hospital and a Lecturer at the University of Zimbabwe. He is also Director of the Fetal Medicine Foundation Zimbabwe and Interim President of the Fetal Medicine Society of Zimbabwe.

Dr Verenga has led the development and decentralisation of fetal medicine and obstetric ultrasound services in Zimbabwe, including establishing public-sector fetal medicine units and training healthcare professionals across the country. His interests include fetal medicine, maternal and perinatal health, medical education, digital health, and scalable models for improving access to specialist care in resource-limited settings.
deepak-saxena:
Dr. Deepak B. Saxena is currently the Director of the Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar (IIPHG) and has over 25 years of experience in public health.

His primary areas of expertise include emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial resistance, One Health, and WASH, along with health systems, community trials, cohort studies, public health innovation, and health technology assessment.

He leads the Centre for One Health Education, Research and Development at IIPHG in collaboration with the University of Bonn. ICMR CCOE for Biomedical research and NIDHI-Technology Business Incubator at IIPHG. He also co-leads the Health Technology Assessment Regional Resource Hub and the Centre of Excellence for Nutrition at IIPHG.

Dr. Saxena has more than 300 publications in peer-reviewed journals and has contributed to scientific research through patents, copyrights, Editorial roles in journals & membership of national and international technical and advisory groups.
daniil-anisimov:
Daniil Anisimov is an AI engineer who builds research agents for drug development. He trained as a physicist at Moscow State University and spent a decade in experimental physics and materials science at the Russian Academy of Sciences, working on semiconductors and sensors, publishing peer-reviewed papers and writing grant proposals.

He then moved from the lab into technology. He co-founded uSense, a hardware startup making air-quality sensors, and Quist, which used large language models to automate literature research and technology due diligence. He now works at Bioptic, a San Francisco startup, building AI agents for teams in pharmaceutical companies who work on drug discovery and drug intelligence.

Daniil has taught AI for scientific research to materials scientists and deep-tech teams. His focus is practical: helping researchers use free AI tools to find gaps, read the literature, analyse data and write, while keeping responsibility for the science.
david-park: Dr. David Park is Managing Director and Head of AI & Strategy at Warren Equity Partners and a Senior Fellow at Columbia University’s Committee on Global Thought. He previously served as a Dean at Columbia University and Senior Vice Provost at Northeastern University and has founded multiple technology startups, including ventures in machine learning and natural language processing. His work sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, investing, and institutional strategy, combining experience as an investor, academic leader, and technology entrepreneur.
diane-kantaros:
Diane Kantaros, MD, FACP, CPE, CPHQ

Dr. Diane Kantaros is an accomplished healthcare leader with over 20 years of hospital-based medicine experience and more than a decade leading quality, safety and clinical operations across a highly matrixed healthcare system. Dr. Kantaros earned her Doctor of Medicine from Albert Einstein College of Medicine and completed her residency at Montefiore Medical Center. She holds board certification in Internal Medicine and has earned credentials including Certified Physician Executive (CPE), Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ), a Certificate in Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare from MIT Sloan Management and is a Certified Master Trainer in High Reliability. She completed the Institute for Healthcare Improvement's Chief Quality Officer Program and sits on the Greater New York Hospital Association AI advisory Committee.

As Chief Quality Officer for Nuvance Health she developed a robust safety program across seven hospitals with measurable, sustained improvements and has worked to introduce AI into clinical practice. Dr. Kantaros has been recognized for her innovation, recently winning an award for an AI prediction model for workplace violence prevention.

Dr. Kantaros leads by combining clinical expertise with strategic vision, a strong technological acumen, and an unwavering commitment to improving patient outcomes and organizational performance.
dilyara-nurkhametova:
Dilyara Nurkhametova, MD, PhD Director of Operations in Global Health, Majid Sadigh, MD Global Health Academy

Dilyara Nurkhametova, MD, PhD, serves as Director of Operations in Global Health at the Majid Sadigh, MD Global Health Academy, where she oversees the operational and educational activities of the Global Health Program. She earned her medical degree with honors from Kazan State Medical University in Russia and completed clinical training in Internal Medicine and Clinical Immunology and Allergology. She later earned a PhD in Molecular Medicine from the University of Eastern Finland.

Dr. Nurkhametova has been involved in global health and international medical education since 2011, with clinical and educational experiences across multiple countries. She joined the Global Health Program in 2016 and has since contributed to the development and coordination of global health electives, international scholar programs, academic initiatives, and research activities. She brings more than a decade of experience in international medical education and global health programming.
douladel-tyndale:
Biography

Douladel Willie-Tyndale, Doctor of Philosophy, Public Health, Post Graduate Diploma, Gerontology (Distinction), Master of Science, Epidemiology

Douladel Willie-Tyndale is a Senior Lecturer and the Director of Mona Ageing and Wellness Centre at The University of the West Indies, Mona Campus in Kingston, Jamaica. In addition to teaching courses in research and gerontology, she coordinates the gerontology programmes offered at the Centre, supervises students at the master’s and doctoral levels, and participates in community outreach activities to educate, support, and empower older adults and their families.

Dr. Willie-Tyndale’s research interests include sexual health, social participation, and health & well-being in midlife and later life.
elvis-novas:
Elvis Novas Brief Bio

Elvis Novas was born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, to Manuel Novas and Mercedes Campos, who taught him to treat others with respect and dignity and to help others whenever he could.

His passion for baseball earned him a scholarship to Universidad Dominicana O&M, where he received a bachelor’s degree in computer science in 1991. While studying, he worked as a computer programmer for CODETEL, the Dominican Republic’s main telephone company.

Elvis moved to the United States in 1992. He lived in New Jersey and New York before moving with his family to Danbury, Connecticut, in 2005. He helped establish the Altamira Softball League in the Bronx and later served as executive secretary of the Latinos Softball League in Danbury. He also co-founded the Dominican Club of Connecticut, which became the Dominican Community Center. He served as its president from 2015 to 2021 and continues to advise the organization.

Elvis also helps organize and teach at the Elvis A. Novas Youth Academy for Leaders, named in memory of his son Elvis Ariel. Through the academy, he works with young people on leadership, civic engagement, financial literacy, and health equity.

Elvis serves as a commissioner of the Housing Authority of the City of Danbury and on the Danbury Zoning Commission. He is also a board member of Housatonic Habitat for Humanity and the Center for Empowerment and Education. His community service has included Brian Cody’s Brothers & Sisters Foundation, which helps people seeking recovery, supports community outreach, and works to reduce the stigma around substance use. In 2018, the U.S. House of Representatives recognized his contributions to civic life with the Latino Leaders in Connecticut Award. He has also received recognition for his work in sports.

A software engineer with more than three decades of experience, Elvis has spent his career developing computer systems and working in information technology. He is the proud father of four children (Mariel, Lisbeth, the late Elvis Ariel, and Aaliyah) and the husband of Zoraida Cabrera.
eric-cioe-pena:
Eric Cioè-Peña MD MPH MBA is the founder and current Vice President of the Center for Global Health of Northwell Health and the Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell, and an Associate Professor of Emergency Medicine. He is a graduate of SUNY Downstate Emergency Medicine Residency program and the Columbia University International Emergency Medicine Fellowship. He received a Master's in Public Health and Humanitarian Assistance from the Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health and received his Doctor of Medicine with concentration in Global Health from the University of Pennsylvania. He received his MBA at Hofstra University.  He served as the ACEP lead ambassador to El Salvador for over a decade. He has worked extensively in Ecuador, Guyana, India, Ukraine, Botswana, Dominican Republic, and El Salvador on health systems development projects, trauma care, and humanitarian assistance.  Dr. Cioè-Peña is a fellow of The Health Management Academy and the American College of Emergency Physicians.  In January, he received the Schwab Foundation’s 2025 Corporate Social Innovator of the Year at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.

Dr. Cioè-Peña is leading the global initiatives at Northwell and Hofstra with a specific focus on stakeholder-led projects centered on access to global mental health, global surgery, and utilization of technology to close health-equity gaps globally as well as to mitigate the effects of climate change on global health. Dr. Cioè-Peña was redeployed in 2020 and 2021 with Northwell at a 108-bed COVID alternate care facility in conjunction with the State of New York as the Medical Director where he directed the care of over 1,000 COVID patients. He is the past president of the Global Emergency Medicine Academy of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine and is also the past president of the Global Emergency Medicine fellowship consortium. He served on the Public Health and Injury Prevention committee.  He has met and been recognized for his work in Global Health by Prime Minister Mia Mottley of Barbados, President Mohamad Irfaan Ali in Guyana and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine.

SHORT VERSION

Eric Cioè-Peña, MD, MPH, MBA is the founder and Vice President of the Center for Global Health at Northwell Health and the Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell, and an Associate Professor of Emergency Medicine. He trained in Emergency Medicine at SUNY Downstate and completed the Columbia University International Emergency Medicine Fellowship, earning an MPH in Humanitarian Assistance from Columbia and an MBA from Hofstra.

He has led health systems development, trauma care, and humanitarian projects in Ecuador, Guyana, India, Ukraine, Botswana, the Dominican Republic, and El Salvador, where he served over a decade as ACEP’s lead ambassador. A fellow of The Health Management Academy and the American College of Emergency Physicians, he was named the Schwab Foundation’s 2025 Corporate Social Innovator of the Year at the World Economic Forum in Davos.

At Northwell, Dr. Cioè-Peña advances global initiatives in mental health, surgery, technology-enabled equity, and climate change mitigation. He served as Medical Director of a 108-bed COVID alternate care facility, treating over 1,000 patients, and is past president of both the Global Emergency Medicine Academy (SAEM) and the Global Emergency Medicine Fellowship Consortium. His global health leadership has been recognized by Prime Minister Mia Mottley of Barbados, President Irfaan Ali of Guyana, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine.

SHORTEST

Eric Cioè-Peña, MD, MPH, MBA is Vice President and founding Director of the Center for Global Health at Northwell Health and Associate Professor of Emergency Medicine at the Zucker School of Medicine. A trained emergency physician with degrees from the University of Pennsylvania, Columbia University, and Hofstra University, he has led health systems, trauma, and humanitarian projects across Latin America, Africa, Asia, and Eastern Europe. He is the 2025 Schwab Foundation Corporate Social Innovator of the Year, recognized globally for advancing mental health, surgery, and technology-driven health equity, and has advised leaders including Prime Minister Mia Mottley of Barbados, President Irfaan Ali of Guyana, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine.

BYLINE VERSION

Eric Cioè-Peña, MD, MPH, MBA is Vice President and founding Director of the Center for Global Health at Northwell Health and Associate Professor of Emergency Medicine at the Zucker School of Medicine. He has led health systems, trauma, and humanitarian initiatives in more than a dozen countries and was named the Schwab Foundation’s 2025 Corporate Social Innovator of the Year. His work focuses on global mental health, surgery, and technology-driven solutions to close health equity gaps worldwide.
eunice-suberu: Eunice Suberu is a final-year medical student at the University of Vermont Larner College of Medicine with interests in global health, health equity, medical education, and child and family well-being. Prior to medical school, she earned a BA in Nutritional Biochemistry and Metabolism and an MS in Nutrition from Case Western Reserve University and worked as a science teacher in a residential program serving youth with complex psychosocial needs. Throughout medical school, her work has included community-engaged projects with immigrant and refugee populations, early childhood social-emotional learning, mentorship and educational initiatives, and research in global health education. She also participated in the GH Elective Program in Vietnam, where she developed a deeper interest in how culture, health systems, and resource availability shape patient care. Across her work, she is particularly interested in strengthening systems that support children and families and in developing sustainable, community-informed approaches to health. She plans to pursue training in child and adolescent psychiatry and hopes to build a career combining clinical care with global mental health, education, and community-centered program development.
ewalina-jeyanesan: Biography Ewalina is a fourth-year medical student passionate about women’s health. Her interest began through early experiences recognizing the stigma and silence surrounding menstruation and women’s reproductive health. As an aspiring obstetrician-gynecologist, Ewalina completed an OB-GYN clinical rotation in Botswana through the Nuvance Global Health Program. Ewalina has held leadership roles at her medical school supporting women in medicine and advocating for enhanced educational opportunities for medical students in Obstetrics and Gynecology. As a principal investigator, she has also led research examining quality of life during pregnancy. A first-generation university graduate and the child of refugees, Ewalina brings a perspective shaped by resilience, cultural humility, and an appreciation for barriers to healthcare. Her goal in medicine is to join the movement to advance compassionate, equitable, patient-centered care for women across diverse communities.
fatumah-ali:
Dr. Nakanwagi Fatumah Ali is an Associate consultant Psychiatrist who has just completed her Master’s of Medicine in Psychiatry training at Makerere University, Uganda, this year.

She is passionate about mental health, particularly addiction psychiatry and is involved in clinical care, advocacy and research.

She is committed to continuous learning, professional development and contributing to mental health awareness and evidence-based practice.
fiona-makoni:
Dr Fiona Makoni

MuDrStom (CSR), MPH (USA), PDG ResEthics (RSA), MScHPE(ZIM)

She has 27 years’ experience in academia and research with the University of Zimbabwe She is the Executive Dean of the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences, University of Zimbabwe. She is a dental surgeon with postgraduate qualifications in public health (USA), research ethics (RSA) and health professions education (ZIM) with experience in curriculum review. She is also a licenced counsellor. She has held various leadership positions in the health sector in Zimbabwe and in her professional association as the first female President of the Zimbabwe Dental Association.  She is dedicated to professional excellence in clinical practice and academia with keen interest in clinical and research ethics, health professions education and global health.
igor-gembitsky:
Name: Igor Gembitsky

Title: Head of Product

Organization: Canary AI Industrial Safety

Igor Gembitsky builds products by understanding what people need and turning emerging technology into practical solutions. His background spans neuroscience research, online education, and more than a decade developing commercial software platforms and leading product teams.

He currently leads product development at Canary, applying AI to industrial safety. Alongside his commercial work, he builds and publishes open-source tools, including an offline virtual patient simulator for medical education.

He is particularly interested in how AI and open-source tools can widen access to learning and healthcare, guided by the needs of the people who use them. His approach connects product strategy, hands-on development, and responsible adoption: choosing worthwhile problems, building with the people affected, and checking whether the results help.
innocent-immaculate-acan: Dr Innocent Immaculate Acan is a Ugandan psychiatrist and global mental health researcher with a particular interest in substance use, bipolar disorder, and the social and structural determinants of mental health in low- and middle-income countries. She recently completed her Master of Medicine in Psychiatry at Makerere University, where her research examined the prevalence and factors associated with substance use disorders among people with bipolar disorder at Butabika National Referral Mental Hospital. As a Rudy Ruggles Global Mental Health Scholar, Dr Acan is interested in developing contextually relevant, evidence-based approaches to improving mental health care in Uganda and across sub-Saharan Africa. Her current research focuses on the relationship between social support and substance use among people living with bipolar disorder, while her broader interests include psychiatric epidemiology, neuropsychiatry, and the translation of global mental health research into locally meaningful clinical practice. She is passionate about strengthening mental health research capacity and developing interventions that are both scientifically rigorous and responsive to the realities of the communities they serve.
jacqueline-cabrera:
Jacqueline Cabrera is a first-generation immigrant and college graduate. She is a community activist and organizer who works directly with the Hands Off CT Coalition to help pass legislation that protects immigrants in Connecticut.

Cabrera has also served as the Coordinator of the Elvis A. Novas Youth Academy. Through her work as Coordinator, she has witnessed students grow from very shy and timid students into confident and knowledgeable young adults.

She is also a member of the Dominican Community Center, where she serves as Vice President. She is the mother of two BIPOC boys who attend Danbury Public Schools. One of her sons, Achilles Peña Cabrera, will be presenting his project at this year’s conference. Jacqueline is proud to have witnessed the growth and development of the students throughout the program. Congratulations to the 2026 class, who will be graduating in June 2027 and continuing their education in college.
jasper-tolarba: Biosketch: Dr. Jasper Erwin Tolarba is an internationally recognized nurse scientist, educator, executive leader, and Fulbright research scholar whose work advances nursing innovation, digital health, workforce development, and global health policy. He currently serves as the Hofstadter-White Endowed Chair of Nursing Practice, Education, Research, and Innovation, and Director of Nursing for the Northwell Global Health Academy of Northwell Health and Sacred Heart University in New York and Connecticut, respectively. Dr. Tolarba earned his Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) from Yale University, obtained a second doctorate (EdD) in education from Columbia University, and completed advanced training in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Data Science at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). An accomplished scholar, Dr. Tolarba has authored numerous peer-reviewed publications in leading nursing journals and has delivered keynote addresses and invited presentations across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Africa. He was also the first foreign educated nurse who became the Director of CGFNS International (now TruMerit) from 2015-2021. A Fellow of the American Academy of Nursing (FAAN), Dr. Tolarba has received numerous honors, including recognition as one of the Top 100 Most Influential Filipinos in the World as well as the Yale School of Nursing Outstanding Decade Alumni Awardee. He also serves as Sigma Nursing's Liaison to the United Nations and spoke in high level meetings of the United Nations.
javier-rincon:
Javier Rincon is a medical student at the Larner College of Medicine, University of Vermont, with an interest in emergency medicine. Before medical school, Javier served in the U.S. Marine Corps as a Combat Engineer, deploying to Iraq and Afghanistan, where he demonstrated strong leadership skills and earned numerous awards for excellence.

Javier's global and community health work spans several initiatives: he has volunteered with the Majid Sadigh, MD Global Health Academy, Bridges to Health, and co-founded the Welcome Immigrant Network, focusing on health disparities and immigrant health support. Most recently, he partnered with the Nuvance Center for Global Health to help improve the EMS system in Guyana, and worked with the Dominican Community Center of Danbury to establish Youth Academy Leaders, a mentorship program for underserved high school students.

Javier holds a B.S. in Biomedical Engineering from Tufts University and brings extensive clinical experience as an EMT and Emergency Department Technician at facilities including Tufts Medical Center and VA San Diego Health Care System. He has also conducted cell culture and tissue engineering research at Tufts, and worked as a Lab Technician at Mass General Brigham performing research in obstructive sleep apnea.
jean-annette-ibo:
Jean Annette S. Ibo

From Legazpi City, Albay, in the Bicol Region of the Philippines.

Completed her Doctor of Education, major in Leadership and Educational Management

With over 26 years of experience in nursing education, with specialization in Community Health Nursing.

Professional involvement extends beyond academia, serving as a trainer for the Municipal Leadership and Governance Program of the Zuellig Family Foundation, where she helped strengthen local health leadership among municipal mayors.

Research contributions include studies on the workplace of Barangay Health Workers in Albay, as well as the knowledge and practices of clients, healthcare providers, and local government units in addressing Pulmonary Tuberculosis and implementing the Directly Observed Treatment Short-Course (DOTS) program

Currently faculty of the Bicol University College of Nursing in Legazpi City.
jerelyn-adviento:
BIOGRAPHY:

Jerelyn B. Adviento, MD, MMHoA, FPCP, FPCC, FPSVM, is an Internal Medicine and  Adult Cardiology,  Peripheral Vascular Medicine specialist. She is  an Associate Professor, the Associate Dean, Overall Program Chair, and Chair of the Curriculum Committee of the Bicol University College of Medicine. She holds a Master’s degree in Hospital Administration and is currently pursuing a PhD in Business Management, major in International Health.

She is actively engaged in postgraduate medical education training in the Bicol Region  as  member of Training  committee for  Adult cardiology and Internal Medicine Training. She also  leads  cardiovascular health advocacy as the  Current President of the Philippine Heart Association – Bicol Chapter

As   the recipient of Global Health Innovations Idea Challenge First Prize 2025, she  leads Project Community HEALS, an  initiatives  that focused on  building solutions for the underserved  and  geographically isolated communities in the Bicol Region. Her global health work includes active participation in international academic partnerships,  and   development of BU Global Health Elective curriculum.

Her interests include preventive cardiology, community health, and development of  socially accountable medical education. Her work focuses  in strengthening the connection between academic medicine and communities, with emphasis on developing sustainable, equitable, and community-responsive approaches to healthcare and medical education.
nankya-josephine:
Personal Introduction

I am Dr. Josephine Nankya, an Associate Consultant Psychiatrist from Uganda and a member of the ISBD Pan African Chapter.

My professional journey in psychiatry has been shaped by a strong interest in improving the quality and accessibility of mental healthcare, particularly for vulnerable and underserved populations.

I have a special interest in mood disorders, especially bipolar disorder, as well as the mental health needs of older adults. My academic and clinical experiences have strengthened my passion for research, lifelong learning, mentorship, and building capacity among mental health professionals.

I am particularly interested in contributing to mental health practice and research within Uganda, Africa, and beyond, while developing into a globally competent psychiatrist.

Outside my professional work, I enjoy spending time with friends, swimming, travelling, exploring new cultures, reading, watching movies, and watching soccer.
joshua-matsiko:
Dr. Joshua Matsiko

Short Biography | GHIIC 2026 PitchFest

────────────────────────────────────────

Dr. Joshua Matsiko is a Ugandan medical doctor, researcher, and health entrepreneur focused on improving access to safe, continuous, and personalized pharmaceutical care. He is the Founder and CEO of Rapharm Ug Ltd, a digital health company integrating pharmacy services, artificial intelligence, medication-safety support, chronic-care follow-up, and last-mile medicine delivery. Through Rapharm, he has led the development of ContinuCare, a pharmacist-led chronic-care model that combines refill support, adherence monitoring, medication review, AI-assisted prescription safety screening, and patient follow-up. Rapharm has served more than 100,000 people and reached users in 91 countries through its digital platforms, while also pioneering technology-enabled last-mile medicine delivery. Dr. Matsiko is a Makerere University-trained medical doctor and is pursuing an MBA at Makerere University. His work has received international recognition through One Young World 2026, Digital Health Africa, and the Africa Impact Challenge (AIC). He is committed to building African health innovations that improve patient safety, strengthen continuity of care, and can be adapted across resource-constrained health systems.

Prepared for the Fifth Annual Global Health Conference – GHIIC 2026
karen-gregorio: Karen Marie R. Gregorio, MD, MPH, FPCP, FPSMID is an Internal Medicine and Infectious Disease Specialist in the Philippines. She is an Associate Professor and College Secretary at the Bicol University College of Medicine and serves as Chief of Clinics and Chair of the Infection Control Committee at UST-Legazpi Hospital. She also chairs infection control committees in other healthcare institutions in the Bicol Region. Dr. Gregorio earned her Doctor of Medicine from the University of Santo Tomas and completed her Internal Medicine residency at Ospital ng Maynila Medical Center and Infectious Diseases fellowship at the University of the Philippines–Philippine General Hospital. She holds a Master of Public Health from the University of the Philippines College of Public Health. Her professional interests include infectious diseases, infection prevention and control, public health, and medical education. She has contributed to national technical working groups that developed Philippine clinical practice guidelines on tuberculosis, adult immunization, urinary tract infections, and opportunistic infections in HIV.
krista-buckley: Dr. Krista Buckley is a board-certified psychiatrist at the University of Vermont Medical Center working clinically in their Primary Care Mental Health Integration division.  She completed her medical degree and residency at the University of Vermont and is happy to be back there as an assistant professor as well as the Associate Residency Director in the Department of Psychiatry.  She is the inaugural Global Mental Health Director and helped establish a global health elective partnership with the University of Botswana.  Her interests are in global mental health, supporting primary care physicians in mental health care, and preventive psychiatry.  She lives in Vermont on a farm with her husband and three children.
lany-maceda:
Dr. Lany L. Maceda, is a seasoned academic leader and researcher holding an academic rank of Professor VI. Under her leadership as the Vice President for Research, Development, and Extension, Bicol University ranked first in the Bicol region for Scopus-indexed research publications in the recent Global Health Focus University Excellence Mid-Year Performance.

Recognized nationally as a Level 2 RD Leader by the Department of Science and Technology-National Research Council of the Philippines (NRCP) and officially conferred as a Scientific and Technological Specialist by the Civil Service Commission. Dr. Maceda focuses on data-driven studies, using computational models and text analytics to convert complex datasets and public feedback into evidence-based decisions. Her research portfolio has over 40 peer-reviewed international publications—garnering 200+ citations.

In addition to her scholarly work, Dr. Maceda brings extensive experience in leading multi-agency research programs and securing major national funding. She currently leads the Department of Budget and Management-funded program entitled, PRIME, to enable assessment of microenterprise vulnerabilities and capacities through their developed technologies that integrate algorithm-based mapping and analytics. She also co-led the Commission on Higher Education funded project, eParticipation 2.1, which analyzed public feedback to strengthen free higher education policies in the Philippines. Her commitment to applied innovation also extends to healthcare through our recently concluded project prototype called BU Health Sync+, an ICT-driven program that aligns with the national goals of Universal Health Care.

Extending her work outside academia, her extension initiatives focused on technology transfer and community empowerment. With 22 registered intellectual properties comprising software products, learning materials, and design patents, Dr. Maceda delivers technical training and data tools to empower local governments, educational institutions, and communities across the Philippines.
linus-chuang:
Linus Chuang, MD, MPH, MS, is a board certified gynecologic oncologist and System Chair of Women’s Health at Northwell Northern Market. He serves as Chair of Obstetrics and Gynecology at Danbury Hospital and holds the Fred and Irmi Bering Endowed Chair in Minimally Invasive Surgery. He is also a Clinical Professor at the University of Vermont Larner College of Medicine.

Dr. Chuang completed his gynecologic oncology fellowship at MD Anderson Cancer Center and has more than 25 years of experience in gynecologic cancer care, minimally invasive and robotic surgery, research, and medical education. He previously held leadership positions at Westchester Medical Center and Mount Sinai Hospital in New York.

Dr. Chuang is actively involved in global gynecologic oncology education and helped develop the International Gynecologic Cancer Society Global Curriculum and Fellowship Program. His academic interests include gynecologic cancer clinical research, minimally invasive surgery, global oncology education, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence in women’s health.
marcos-nunez:

maria-della-c-raneses:
BIOGRAPHY

MARIA DELLA C. RAÑESES, PhD, PhD, PhD

Professor IV

Dr. Maria Della C. Rañeses is a Filipino nurse educator, researcher, and academic leader currently serving as the Dean of the Bicol University College of Nursing in Legazpi City, Albay. A Professor IV, she is recognized for her distinguished academic credentials, having earned three doctoral degrees and two master's degrees, reflecting her unwavering commitment to lifelong learning, scholarly excellence, and professional leadership.

Throughout her career, she has dedicated herself to advancing nursing education, research, extension, and institutional development. Dr. Rañeses has authored and co-authored a few peer-reviewed research publications focusing on nursing education, community health, lifestyle and wellness, psychosocial health, non-communicable diseases, and solo parenting.

As Dean of the Bicol University College of Nursing, Dr. Rañeses provides strategic leadership in strengthening academic programs, promoting research and innovation, expanding community engagement, and fostering local and international partnerships.
mariah-mcnamara:
Mariah McNamara, MD, MPH, FACEP Associate Professor of Emergency Medicine | Vice Chair for Clinical Affairs | Associate Chief Medical Officer, University of Vermont Health

Dr. Mariah McNamara is a physician-leader whose career exemplifies the intersection of clinical excellence, global health advocacy, and institutional leadership. As Vice Chair for Clinical Affairs in the Department of Emergency Medicine at the University of Vermont’s Larner College of Medicine and Associate Chief Medical Officer for the UVM Health Network, she oversees medical staff services across a six-hospital system, guiding credentialing, privileging, and peer review at a system level.

A graduate of the University of Vermont and Harvard University, Dr. McNamara brings a health systems perspective to her work, shaped by her MPH in International Health and a fellowship in Global Emergency Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital. She has led transformative initiatives and made contributions to scholarship in emergency department operations, crisis response, and health equity, including during the COVID-19 pandemic and a major cyberattack.

Dr. McNamara is also a passionate educator and mentor, having served as Interim Assistant Dean for Students and Associate Director of the Global Health Program. She has developed innovative curricula, mentored emerging leaders, and championed inclusive, community-engaged medical education. Her leadership reflects a commitment to service, collaboration, and professional development in medicine and health systems leadership.
sula-matovu-ntanda: Dr. Sula Matovu is a Ugandan medical doctor, healthcare advocate, and health innovation enthusiast with eight years of experience delivering patient-centered care in resource-limited settings. He currently serves at St. Stephen’s Hospital, Mpererwe, a partner site of Nuvance Health, where he combines frontline clinical practice with leadership in community health initiatives. His work has spanned HIV/AIDS, sickle cell disease, maternal health, noncommunicable diseases, and health education, including leading an AstraZeneca-funded initiative that screened more than 3000 people for chronic kidney disease. Beyond the clinic, Dr. Matovu is a passionate health communicator. His Tiktok based digital health education content has reached more than 100,000 Ugandans, and he is the author of Maama Care: Your Pregnancy Guide from A to Z. His passion for health equity and digital innovation motivated him to come up with CareLink—a mobile and enterprise telemedicine platform designed to connect rural Ugandan patients with urban-based specialists to reduce waiting times that may span into months before a patient can meet a specialist in a country where the doctor to patient ratio is 1:25,000- a ratio that’s abysmally low compared a WHO recommended ratio of 1 doctor per 1,000 patients.
ninoska-abreu-placeres: Ninoska Abreu Placeres, is Director of the Biomaterials and Dentistry Research Center (CIBO) at Universidad Iberoamericana (UNIBE) in the Dominican Republic, where she is also a faculty member and researcher. She holds a PhD in Dental Sciences with a focus on Cariology from the University of Copenhagen, a Master’s degree in Dental Sciences from Universidad El Bosque, and specialty training in Pediatric Dentistry from Universidad del Salvador. Her research focuses on cariology, oral health, dental education, and the development and evaluation of innovative approaches for caries prevention, diagnosis, and management. She is Vice President of the Caribbean Oral Health Initiative (COHI) and is actively involved in regional and international collaborations aimed at strengthening oral health research, education, and public health in Latin America and the Caribbean.
ofelia-samar-sy:
Dr. Ofelia M. Samar-Sy is an internist and cardiologist who has taught in medical schools since completing postgraduate training. She has served as dean of three medical schools and now leads Bicol University College of Medicine in the Philippines.

Raised in a family of modest means, she earned her medical degree through a state scholarship. She chairs the Bicol University College of Medicine (BUCM) Committee on Scholarship, supporting students from underprivileged backgrounds who are preparing to serve remote communities. Her work in Bicol, a region affected by typhoons and disasters, informs her approach to medical education, community health, and collaboration.
pamela-jimenez-taveras: Pamela Jiménez Taveras serves as Coordinator of Visiting Students at Universidad Iberoamericana (UNIBE) in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. She oversees international student mobility programs, supports global partnerships, and promotes intercultural learning experiences for students and faculty. Her work focuses on fostering cross-cultural understanding and strengthening international collaboration in higher education.
patricia-grau-grullon: Patricia Grau Grullón, DDS, MSc, PhD, is a dentist, university professor, and researcher from the Dominican Republic with more than 20 years of experience in dental education, research, and clinical practice. She is a professor at the School of Dentistry of Universidad Iberoamericana (UNIBE), where she teaches undergraduate and postgraduate students, and is a researcher at the Center for Research in Biomaterials and Dentistry (CIBO). She earned her DDS, Cum Laude, from UNIBE, an MSc in Restorative Dentistry and Dental Materials from the State University of Ponta Grossa, Brazil, and a PhD in Dentistry, with a focus on Biomaterials, from the Federal University of Pelotas, Brazil. Her academic interests include dental biomaterials, restorative dentistry, light-curing, and dental education. She has authored and co-authored scientific articles in international peer-reviewed journals and has presented her research and delivered lectures at national and international scientific and professional meetings.
quoc-bao-nguyen:
Quoc Bao Nguyen is a upper-year Pharmacy student at the University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City, specializing in Pharmaceutical Informatics and healthcare innovation. Positioned at the intersection of medical science, marketing strategy, and creative arts, he brings a unique, multidisciplinary perspective to brand building and digital storytelling.

Quoc Bao has demonstrated proven leadership and strategic thinking as a finalist in several national and global health innovation challenges, including the Global Health Innovation Idea Challenge (GHIIC) and AstraZeneca Project iDEA. Beyond his academic pursuits, he actively integrates creative content strategy and visual communications into healthcare projects to bridge the gap between complex medical science and public engagement.

Driven by a commitment to social impact, Quoc Bao aims to leverage digital innovation and interdisciplinary collaboration to improve community health accessibility and build sustainable healthcare ecosystems.
ricardo-isip:
RICARDO D. ISIP JR. MD.MHA, FPPAI, FPAAS, FPFCS

General and Cosmetic Surgery

Dr. Ricardo Isip Jr. is a distinguished leader in surgery, medical education, and aesthetic medicine. A fellow and diplomate of the Pan Pacific Aesthetic Institute and the Philippine Federation of Cosmetic Surgeons, he brings extensive expertise to his diverse leadership roles.

Dr. Isip serves as the Department Chair of Surgical Specialties and an Associate Professor at Bicol University College of Medicine.He provides specialized care as a Surgical Consultant at UST HospitalLegazpi and Albay Doctors Hospital, a Cosmetic Surgery Consultant

at ACE Medical Center Legazpi, and is the founder and Medical Director of I-Slim & Skin Aesthetic Center.

He has held significant leadership positions, including Past President of the Albay Medical Society and Past Philippine Medical Association Governor for the Bicol Region.

Dr. Isip is also actively involved in international medical societies, including the Asian Facial Plastic Surgery Society and Asia Pacific Anti Aging Society in Korea, and the International Society for Stem Cell Silurgery in the USA and Canada. He is also a member of the Philippine Society of Liposuction Surgery and anAssociate Fellow of the Philippine Academy of Aesthetic Surgery. He holds a Doctor of Medicine degree and a Master of Health Administration currently doing hid thesis for his PhD in International Health Management.
robert-kalyesubula: Dr Kalyesubula, MBChB, Mmed, FISN(USA), PhD, FRCP I am currently Senior Lecturer in department of Medicine and Chair, Physiology, Makerere University College of Health Science and an Adjunct Ass. Clinical Professor at Yale School of Medicine, USA. ruby-espares:
BIOGRAPHY

Ruby D. Espares, Ph.D is a Registered Nurse and Licensed Professional Teacher in the Philippines, with over 14 years of experience in nursing education and clinical practice. She currently serves as an Instructor 1 in the Nursing Department of Bicol University Tabaco, Philippines, where she teaches Pharmacology and Medical-Surgical Nursing and serves as the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) Level 1 Coordinator.

Prior to her academic career, Dr. Espares served as Chief Nurse of Jaime B. Berces Memorial Hospital, gaining experience in clinical leadership, nursing administration, and patient care. She is committed to developing future nurses through meaningful classroom, laboratory, and clinical learning experiences.

She holds a PhD in Educational Foundation and a Master of Arts in Nursing. Her current academic work includes developing instructional materials in Pharmacology to support self-directed and clinically relevant learning among nursing students. Her professional interests include nursing education, instructional development, and clinical practice.

sandra-lindsay:
Dr. Sandra L. Lindsay, a Presidential Medal of Freedom Recipient, the nation’s highest civilian honor made history on December 14, 2020, as the first person in the United States to receive the COVID-19 vaccine outside clinical trials, becoming a powerful beacon of hope and trust.

Currently, Dr. Lindsay serves as Vice President of Public Health Advocacy at Northwell Health, where she champions initiatives to reduce health disparities, improve access to care, and advance health equity. Her commitment to advancing health equity extends globally, beginning with her unwavering dedication to improving women's health in her native Jamaica. She has been instrumental in spearheading annual life-changing surgical missions to provide pro bono surgical interventions for women in the public health system. Through her Sandra Lindsay Foundation, she spearheads the "Dignity for All" initiative, providing young girls with ongoing access to essential menstrual health products. resources and education.

Dr. Lindsay's influence is extensive. She inspires others through speaking engagements and mentorship. Her memoir, "First in Line, How COVID-19 placed Me on the Frontlines of a Health Care Crisis" details her extraordinary journey. A proud immigrant, Sandra credits her upbringing for instilling the values of caring and sharing.
shushanik-isahakyan:
Shushanik Isahakyan is the Head of the International Cooperation Department at the National Institute of Health of Armenia and Co-Director of the Nuvance Health Global Health Program for the Armenia site. She is committed to strengthening healthcare in Armenia through local and international collaboration.

Shushanik holds a BA in Economic Theory and an MA in International Economics from Yerevan State University and is currently pursuing her PhD in International Economics.

She has extensive experience working on international health projects with major organizations, including the World Bank, WHO, ADB, USAID, and UNAIDS. Her responsibilities include developing and managing partnerships, coordinating collaborative projects, and supporting international initiatives aligned with Armenia’s healthcare priorities and global health standards.

Shushanik is also involved in health research and has authored numerous publications. Her work focuses on strengthening healthcare systems, improving health services, and supporting the exchange of knowledge and expertise.

Through her work, Shushanik builds connections between Armenia and the international health community, creating opportunities for collaboration, education, and knowledge exchange. She is committed to supporting the development of Armenia’s healthcare system and contributing to better quality of care and health outcomes.
stanley-kowalski: Stanley Kowalski III Entrepreneur | Inventor | University Trustee Stanley Kowalski III is an entrepreneur, inventor, and mechanical engineer whose career spans life sciences, clean energy, and the commercialization of university research. He co-founded and served as CEO of FloDesign Sonics, developing acoustic cell-processing technology to support the manufacture of cell and gene therapies, and was the founding CEO of FloDesign Wind Turbine. A graduate and trustee of Western New England University, he has helped connect academic research with industry while creating opportunities for students and emerging entrepreneurs. Through his involvement with the Global Health Academy, Stanley brings a practical entrepreneurial perspective to how artificial intelligence and emerging technologies can expand access to expertise, support innovation, and translate promising ideas into meaningful improvements in global health.
tracy-evans-gilbert:
Dr. Evans- Gilbert is a graduate of the  University of the West Indies ,studied  clinical research at Johns Hopkins University and Tropical Medicine at  West Virginia University .

She is a Senior Associate Lecturer , clinical researcher and Consultant in Paediatrics, Tropical Medicine and Public Health   at the University of the West Indies, Jamaica, and a clinical preceptor for  for global health  students from the West Virginia University at the Cornwall Regional Hospital. She serves on local regional and international advisory boards concerning childhood infectious diseases and immunization policy and has published 50 research papers focused on childhood tropical diseases.
xavier-brown: Biography Dr. Xavier Brown is a Consultant Obstetrician and Gynaecologist with a specialized focus on Minimal Access Surgery. He completed both his undergraduate and postgraduate degrees at the University of the West Indies, Jamaica. Dr. Brown currently practices at the University Hospital of the West Indies and the Connolley Health & Wellness Centre, both situated in Kingston, Jamaica. His services encompass a wide range of areas, including pregnancy care, vaginal deliveries, cesarean sections, fibroid management, postnatal care, obstetric ultrasounds, family planning and contraception methods, management of abnormal uterine bleeding, hysterectomies (both traditional and laparoscopic), minimal access surgeries (camera-assisted procedures), management of ovarian cysts, infertility, endometriosis, chronic pelvic pain, and many other facets of women’s health. Dr. Brown is deeply committed to advancing Women's Health Care in Jamaica. Outside of his professional commitments, he is a devoted husband and father of three, cherishing the time spent with his family while striving to balance his dedication to both his practice and his loved ones.
christina-laird:

chuchard-punsawad:
Biography of Dr. Chuchard Punsawad

Assoc. Prof. Dr. Chuchard Punsawad is the Dean of the School of Medicine, Walailak University, Thailand, and an Associate Professor in Parasitology. He received his Ph.D. in Tropical Medicine from Mahidol University. His research focuses on malaria, parasitic diseases, tropical medicine, and the development of medicinal plants and natural products for the treatment of parasitic infections. He has published extensively in international journals and is actively involved in medical education, research, postgraduate supervision, and international academic collaboration. As Dean, he is committed to advancing medical education, research and innovation, and global partnerships in health sciences.
cosima-neumann: Dr. Cosima Neumann is an OBGYN who just completed her residency at Danbury Hospital, Northwell Health in June, 2026 and will be starting as an OBGYN Generalist at New York University. She has a passion for Global Women’s Health and was able to practice internationally twice during residency - on the island of Grenada to perform pro bono benign GYN surgeries through the McKinney Foundation and in Botswana for a 4-week OBGYN elective through the Botswana Harvard Partnership and the Global Health Department.
kevin-dieckhaus:
Kevin Dieckhaus MD FIDSA CTropMed®

Professor of Medicine

Professor of Public Health Sciences

Chief, Division of Infectious Diseases

Director of Global Health & International Studies

University of Connecticut School of Medicine

Farmington, Connecticut, USA

Kevin D. Dieckhaus, MD is Professor of Medicine, Director of Global Health and International Studies, and Chief of the Division of Infectious Diseases at the UConn School of Medicine.

Dr. Dieckhaus completed his Medical Schooling at the University of Missouri-Kansas City, Internal Medicine training at Yale-New Haven Hospital, and Infectious Diseases fellowship at the University of Connecticut. He is the Chief of the Division of Infectious Diseases, Director of Global Health and International Studies, and Director of International Travel Medicine and Immunization Services at UConn Health Center.

He leads the University of Connecticut's HIV/AIDS support services to improve and enhance the medical care and address medical and economic inequities of the HIV/AIDS populations in Central Connecticut. He teaches microbiology, parasitology, infectious diseases, and community research methodologies at the UConn School of Medicine.

He has been an active educator for HIV medicine locally at the UConn School of Medicine, statewide, and internationally. He is the medical director for the Clare Nsenga Foundation, a 501-c3 charitable organization that operates a rural medical clinic, maternity center, and associated public health‐related outreach programs in Kisoro, Uganda, and volunteers regularly as a visiting physician at the St. Francis Hospital in Mutolere, Uganda.

Research interests are varied and have included topics in international travel medicine, tropical diseases, infectious diseases, health care delivery in developing areas, and educational methodologies.  Recent projects have focused on malaria, rheumatic heart disease, syphilis, dengue, brucellosis, perinatal health care, use of baby boxes as a perinatal intervention in LMICs, antibiotic stewardship in Travel Medicine, babesiosis, determinants of health in HIV populations, and clinical impact of respiratory syncytial virus in the USA. He coordinates local and international research experiences for medical students and residents at the University of Connecticut school of medicine.
nonthapan-phasuk:
Assoc. Prof. Nonthapan Phasuk, MD’s biography

Assoc. Prof. Nonthapan Phasuk, MD, is the Vice Dean of the School of Medicine at Walailak University, Thailand, where she also serves as the Program Director for the Doctor of Medicine program. She specializes in pediatric infectious diseases and her research focuses on bacterial and parasitic infections in children.

She is dedicated to elevating medical education through curriculum innovation, focusing on the clinical integration of preclinical medical students to align with global WFME standards. Through her administrative and pedagogical efforts, Dr. Phasuk works to bridge early basic sciences with practical healthcare, ensuring high-quality teaching, and professional excellence for the next generation of physicians at Walailak University.
pirada-yincharoen:
Biography

Pirada Yincharoen, MD

Dr. Pirada Yincharoen is a breast surgeon and faculty member at the School of Medicine, Walailak University, Thailand. Her clinical and research interests include breast surgical oncology, oncoplastic surgery, multidisciplinary cancer care, and patient-centered decision-making.

She completed her General Surgery training at Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, followed by a clinical fellowship in Head, Neck, and Breast Surgery. She has further developed her expertise through international training, including an observership in oncoplastic breast surgery at Oxford University Hospitals in the United Kingdom.

In 2025, Dr. Yincharoen joined the Global Health Academy’s Global Health Scholar Program in Breast and Reconstructive Surgery at Nuvance Health in Connecticut and subsequently completed an observership in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center in New York. Her current work focuses on breast cancer research, surgical education, and fostering international collaboration and cross-cultural learning in global health.
sunaina-rao: Sunaina Rao is Chief Neurology Resident at Northwell Health Vassar Brothers Medical Center. As a PGY-3 resident, she was part of her program’s first cohort to complete a global health elective in Botswana and now serves as its curriculum lead. She is especially passionate about increasing global awareness of headache disorders and reducing the stigma surrounding them. She will begin her Headache Medicine fellowship at Thomas Jefferson University next year.
michelle-lea:
Biography

Michelle Lea, DMSc, PA-C joined the University of Bridgeport Physician Assistant Institute following a distinguished 20-year career in the United States Navy. She is a board-certified Physician Assistant with over 16 years of clinical experience specializing in emergency and urgent care medicine. She earned her Master of Science in Physician Assistant Studies from the Interservice Physician Assistant Program at the University of Nebraska Medical Center in 2010 and her Doctor of Medical Science in Medical Education from the University of Lynchburg in 2026.

During her military career, Dr. Lea served in a variety of operational and leadership roles around the world. In 2011, she deployed to Afghanistan in support of Operation Enduring Freedom, where she served with a Provincial Reconstruction Team focused on healthcare capacity building and public health initiatives. She was subsequently selected to serve with the White House Medical Unit during the Obama administration as the Medical Officer for Camp David, providing primary and acute care to the President, Vice President, their families, and White House personnel.

Following completion of the Navy's 18-month Emergency Medicine Physician Assistant Fellowship at Naval Medical Center San Diego, Dr. Lea was selected to serve as Program Director of the fellowship, where she led postgraduate physician assistant education, curriculum development, and faculty mentorship. She continues to practice clinically in urgent care and serves as an Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant (ARC-PA) site visitor.

Dr. Lea joined the University of Bridgeport Physician Assistant Institute in 2021 and currently serves as Director of Clinical Education and Assistant Professor. Her scholarly interests include preparing future clinicians to care for medically underserved and vulnerable populations through innovative clinical training experiences.
